title: The Vertex Formula
short: The vertex of ax² + bx + c is at x = −b/(2a).
trouble: Students drop the negative sign, using x = b/(2a).

blocks.html: In Algebra 1 you found the vertex by completing the square. That works every time, but it is slow. Doing it once with letters instead of numbers gives a formula you can use directly.

The vertex of $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ is at $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$. Substitute that $x$ back into the function to get the $y$-coordinate. The axis of symmetry is the line $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$, and the vertex height is the minimum value when $a > 0$ and the maximum when $a < 0$.

Complete the square on $ax^2 + bx + c$ with letters. Factor $a$ out of the first two terms: $a\left(x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x\right) + c$. Half of $\frac{b}{a}$ is $\frac{b}{2a}$, so $$x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x = \left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 - \frac{b^2}{4a^2}.$$ The squared part is smallest (zero) when $x + \frac{b}{2a} = 0$, that is, at $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$. There is another way to see it: the zeros of $ax^2 + bx$ are $0$ and $-\frac{b}{a}$, and the vertex sits halfway between them. Adding $c$ moves the parabola up or down but not sideways.

blocks.title: A maximum value
blocks.q: A ball's height is $h(t) = -16t^2 + 48t + 5$ feet after $t$ seconds. What is its greatest height?
steps: $a = -16 < 0$, so the parabola opens down and the vertex is the highest point.

blocks.html: Dropping the negative sign and using $x = \frac{b}{2a}$. For $y = x^2 - 6x$ that puts the vertex at $x = -3$ instead of $x = 3$. Check: the zeros of $x^2 - 6x$ are 0 and 6, and the vertex must be halfway between them, at $x = 3$.
